comment: There is no right of access for participants anywhere in the guidance. Public governance protects the infrastructure from capture by a single programme, donor or vendor, but nothing protects an individual participant - a provider, a regional collaborative, a small vendor - from being refused, delayed or charged differently by whoever operates the shared component. A duty to connect without a right to connect is an obligation to become dependent on a party that may refuse.

public.text: There is no right of access for participants anywhere in the guidance. Public governance protects the infrastructure from capture by a single programme, donor or vendor, but nothing protects an individual participant - a provider, a regional collaborative, a small vendor - from being refused, delayed or charged differently by whoever operates the shared component. A duty to connect without a right to connect is an obligation to become dependent on a party that may refuse.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a right to connect as a DPI-H principle: any conformant participant may connect to a DPI-H component on published, non-discriminatory terms, within a defined lead time, with a route of appeal if refused or delayed. This mirrors third-party access in other regulated infrastructure and is, in Ostrom's terms, recognition of the right to organise. For small providers the right should be exercisable collectively, through a vendor or collaborative connecting on their behalf, with the cost carried in the tariff rather than in their own budget.
